name: Talia Valdez
life: “One of my pupils went on tour and mailed me a different terrible hotel pen each week.” On Friday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Talia notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I taught two pupils on that horn. Neither ever knew I owned it first.
appearance: Talia has steel-colored hair cut square above the collar, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a gray fisher's sweater. It usually goes with a seam let out by a narrow strip of contrasting fabric. When somebody else has the floor, Talia looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry.
personality: Talia keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Talia wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To let two generations of students meet at rehearsal.
family: Francis Parra is Talia’s stepsibling. Talia calls about good news first. Francis is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *The kitchen without a boss*, Francis says, “I have shares and no apron. I offered to carry flour for one afternoon before looking at the daily numbers.”
connections: Erin Hubbard. Two teachers recognize two different stages of the trumpet's working life.

reactions.situation: The teenager gets an audition the morning the horn is due back
reactions.response: Talia contacts the owner before treating an audition as permission to keep the horn.

reactions.response: Talia asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Talia offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
